### Files in C – A Quick Overview In C, **files** are external storage objects you read from or write to through the Standard I/O Library (`stdio.h`). A *file* is simply a sequence of bytes stored outside your program’s memory—on disk, flash, network socket, etc.—that persists after the program ends. --- #### 1. Why Use Files? | Reason | What You Get | |--------|--------------| | Persist data beyond runtime | Store configuration, logs, databases, media, etc. | | Handle larger-than‑RAM datasets | Read/write chunks instead of loading everything at once | | Interact with other programs | Share information via common formats | --- #### 2. Core Concepts & Types | Concept | Description | |---------|-------------| | `FILE` object | An opaque structure representing an open stream. Declared in ``. | | Stream type | Text vs Binary
`fopen()`’s `"r"` / `"w"` → text (newline translation).
`"rb"` / `"wb"` → raw binary. | | Buffering | Automatic line/buffered reads/writes improve performance.
Use `setvbuf()` to control buffer size/type. | | File descriptor | Low‑level integer returned by OS APIs (`_open`, `_creat`) used internally by `FILE`. Not directly exposed unless you call `fileno(FILE*)`. | --- #### 3. Opening & Closing Streams ```c #include int main(void) { /* Open a file for reading */ FILE *fp = fopen("data.txt", "r"); // "r": read-only, text mode if (!fp) { perror("fopen failed"); return 1; } /* ...use fp... */ fclose(fp); // Close when finished } ``` Common flags: | Mode | Meaning | |------|---------| | `"r"` | Read only, text | | `"w"` | Write only, truncate/create | | `"a"` | Append, create if missing | | `"b"` | Binary flag (appended to above) | | `"+"` | Update (read+write) | Example: `"rb+"` opens existing file for both reading and writing without truncation. --- #### 4. Reading & Writing Data ##### Text Functions | Function | Purpose | Example | |----------|---------|---------| | `fprintf()` | Formatted output to a stream | `fprintf(fp, "%d %s\n", id, name);` | | `fscanf()` | Scanned input from a stream | `if(fscanf(fp,"%d",&id)==1){ … }` | | `gets()/puts()` | Legacy, unsafe; avoid! | | `getline()` | Dynamically allocate buffer for a whole line | `char *line=NULL; getline(&line,&len,fp);` | ##### Binary Functions | Function | Purpose | Example | |----------|---------|---------| | `fread()` | Read blocks into memory | `size_t n= fread(buf,sizeof(char),N,fp);` | | `fwrite()` | Write blocks from memory | `fwrite(data,sizeof(DataStruct),cnt,fp);` | | `ftell()` | Current position (in bytes) | `long pos = ftell(fp);` | | `fseek()` | Move to arbitrary offset | `fseek(fp,0L,SEEK_END);` | | `rewind()` | Reset to start | `rewind(fp);` | --- #### 5. Error Handling All I/O functions set `errno` upon failure. Check return values carefully: ```c if (ferror(fp)) { perror("I/O error"); } ``` For formatted input, check number of items successfully matched. --- #### 6. Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | Mixing text and binary incorrectly | Keep consistent mode per platform | | Forgetting to close files | Always `fclose()` or rely on automatic cleanup at exit | | Using `gets()` | Replace with safer alternatives (`fgets`, `getline`) | | Ignoring `feof()` before checking errors | Call `feof()` only after a failed read attempt | --- #### 7. Sample Program – Copying a File ```c /* copy.c - copies src.bin to dst.bin byte-by-byte */ #include #include #define BUF_SIZE 4096 int main(int argc,char *argv[]) { if(argc!=3){ fprintf(stderr,"Usage: %s source dest\n", argv[0]); return EXIT_FAILURE; } FILE *src=fopen(argv[1],"rb"), *dst=fopen(argv[2],"wb"); if(!src||!dst){ perror("fopen"); return EXIT_FAILURE;} char buf[BUF_SIZE]; size_t n; while((n=fread(buf,1,BUF_SIZE,src))){ fwrite(buf,1,n,dst); } fclose(src); fclose(dst); printf("Copy completed.\n"); return EXIT_SUCCESS; } ``` Compile with `gcc copy.c -o copy`. --- #### 8. Advanced Topics (Optional) - **Memory-mapped files** (`mmap` on POSIX, `CreateFileMapping` + `MapViewOfFile` on Win32) - **Thread-safe I/O** (`lock_file`, `unlock_file`) - **Non-blocking I/O** (`select`, `poll`, overlapped IO on Windows) - **Locale-aware formatting** (`localeconv()`) --- ### TL;DR - In C, a *file* is accessed via a `FILE*` stream opened with `fopen`. - Choose correct mode (`"r"/"w"/"a"+` plus optional `"b"`). - Use `fread`/`fwrite` for binary, `fprintf`/`fscanf` for formatted text. - Always check return codes and close with `fclose`. Happy coding!
